q.q: In a two-candidate election 5% of the 20000 votes cast were invalid. The winner got 60% of the valid votes. By how many votes did he win?
q.e: Valid votes = 19000; margin = 20% of 19000 = 3800.

q.q: The present ages of A and B are in the ratio 7:6. After 10 years the ratio will be 9:8. What is the sum of their present ages?
From a point on level ground the angle of elevation of the top of a tower is 30°. On walking 30 m towards the tower along level ground, the angle of elevation becomes 60°. The height of the tower is:

In a group, 41 students like cricket, 31 like football and 71 like hockey; 18 like cricket and football, 16 like football and hockey, 9 like hockey and cricket, and 6 like all three games. Every student likes at least one game. How many students like exactly two of the games?
q.e: Exactly two = Σpairs − 3·(all three) = 43 − 18 = 25.

q.q: If α and β are the roots of x² − 6x + 7 = 0, then α⁴ + β⁴ equals:
q.e: Use α+β = 6, αβ = 7; value = 386.

q.q: The point which divides the line segment joining A(-2, -6) and B(-4, -5) internally in the ratio 3:1 is:
q.e: Section formula: (3x₂+1x₁)/(3+1), (3y₂+1y₁)/(3+1).

q.q: How many digits does 4^70 have?
q.e: Digits = ⌊70 log 4⌋ + 1 = 43.

q.q: In an arithmetic progression the 5th term is 29 and the 7th term is 41. The sum of its first 25 terms is:
A pipe fills a tank in 12 hours. Because of a leak at the bottom the tank takes 13 hours to fill. In how many hours would the leak alone empty the full tank?
q.e: Leak rate = 1/12 − 1/13; time = 156 hours.

q.q: A loan is repaid in 3 equal annual instalments of Rs 6000 each, the first one due one year after the loan, with interest at 25% per annum compounded annually. The amount of the loan was:
A, B and C can complete a work in 20, 15 and 12 days respectively. They are paid Rs 6000 in total for completing it together. What is C's share (in rupees), in proportion to the work done?
The radii of the ends of a frustum of a cone are 10 cm and 6 cm and its height is 3 cm. Its volume is (in cm³):
q.e: Slant height = √(3²+4²) = 5 cm; use π(R+r)l or πh(R²+Rr+r²)/3.

q.q: A bag contains 4 red, 6 blue and 2 green balls. Three balls are drawn at random without replacement. The probability that one ball of each colour is drawn is:
A man walking at 3 km/h reaches his office 30 minutes late, while walking at 12 km/h he reaches 15 minutes early. The distance to his office (km) is:
If '+' means '+', '−' means '−', '×' means '÷', '÷' means '×', then the value of 20 − 11 + 3 + 6 is:
q.e: Replace each sign by its meaning: 20 − 11 + 3 + 6 = 18 (BODMAS applies).

q.q: After 12 o'clock, at how many minutes past 12 do the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock first make an angle of 90° with each other?
q.e: 5.5m = 30·12 ± 90 (mod 360); the first positive solution is m = 16 4/11 minutes.

q.q: Ayesha is the mother of Amna. Amna is the daughter of Jamil. Jamil is the son of Salman. Salman is the husband of Kiran. How is Ayesha related to Kiran?
q.e: Work through the chain link by link, assuming the usual convention that a couple's children are common to both.

q.q: Statement: U > V = Y ≤ Q = S > P. Conclusions: I. U > S  II. V ≤ U  III. Y < P. Which of the conclusions is/are definitely true?
o: Only II and III are true
Only I and II are true
q.e: A conclusion is definitely true only if it holds for every set of values consistent with the whole chain.

q.q: In a row, Imran is 17th from the left end and Junaid is 13th from the right end. If they interchange positions, Imran becomes 24th from the left. How many persons are there in the row?
q.e: After the exchange Imran is at Junaid's old place: 24 from the left and 13 from the right, so total = 24+13−1.

q.q: What is the value of x? (x and y are positive integers.) I. x + 2y = 56. II. x is 30.
o: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither alone is
Even both statements together are not sufficient
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
q.e: Test each statement alone, then both together, by checking whether exactly one value of the unknown remains.

q.q: 5 people sit in a row from left to right. Each has a different job (banker, doctor, farmer, pilot, teacher) and a different city (Karachi, Lahore, Multan, Quetta, Sukkur). The person whose job is doctor has city Lahore. The person with job banker sits immediately to the left of the person with city Karachi. The person whose job is pilot has city Multan. The person with job doctor sits at the left end. The person with job farmer sits at the right end. The person whose job is teacher has city Sukkur. The person with job doctor sits next to the person with city Sukkur. Which city belongs to the person with job teacher?
q.e: Place the fixed-position clues first, then combine the matching clues; only one arrangement satisfies them all.

q.q: Statements: All birds are clocks. Some birds are coins. Some rivers are coins. Conclusions: I. No coin is a river.  II. Some coins are birds.  III. Some clocks are rivers.  IV. No clock is a bird. Which of the conclusions definitely follow(s)?
o: Only I, II and IV follow
q.e: Draw all possible Venn diagrams for the three statements; a conclusion follows only if it holds in every one of them.

q.q: In a certain code, CODE is written as 19 and PACK is written as 180. How will MANGO be written in that code?
q.e: The code is the alphabet position of the first letter times that of the last, plus the number of letters; MANGO → 200.

q.q: How many Saturdays are there in April 2034?
q.e: April 2034 has 30 days; counting the Saturdays gives 5.

q.q: 6 students Asad, Faraz, Nida, Rabia, Sara, Zainab each have a test on a different day, from Monday to Saturday (one test per day). Nida's test is held earlier in the week than Rabia's. Exactly 3 days separate Faraz's test and Sara's. Nida's test is held on the day immediately before Asad's. Exactly 2 days separate Rabia's test and Asad's. Exactly 4 days separate Sara's test and Rabia's. On which day is Zainab's test held?
q.e: Place the definite clues first (immediate neighbours, ends), then use the 'between' and 'left of' clues to fix the rest; the arrangement is unique.
Rule: n → n² + n; 12 → 156.
